A320-200
Airbus A320-200 aircraft model covered by the Aircraft Characteristics manual for airport and maintenance planning.<SEP>Airbus A320-200 aircraft model covered by the Airport and Maintenance Planning documentation.<SEP>Airbus A320-200 aircraft model covered by the Airport and Maintenance Planning document.

A320neo
Airbus A320neo aircraft model covered by the Aircraft Characteristics manual for airport and maintenance planning.<SEP>Airbus A320neo aircraft model covered by the Airport and Maintenance Planning documentation.<SEP>Airbus A320neo aircraft model covered by the Airport and Maintenance Planning document.

Ground Service Connections Layout
Diagram and listing of ground service connection points for the A320-200 and A320

Wing
Aircraft wing structure containing front spar, ribs, refuel point, and grounding points.

Front Spar
Primary structural member of the wing located at the front.

Rib19
Wing rib number 19, a structural component of the wing.

Rib20
Wing rib number 20, a structural component of the wing.

Refuel Point
Ground service connection on the wing upper surface for refueling; not available on some aircraft.

Grounding Point
Earthing connection point on the aircraft structure for electrical grounding; also labeled "GROUND HERE" on some aircraft.

Avionics Compartment Door-Frame
Door frame of the avionics compartment equipped with a grounding (earthing) point.

Engine Air Intake
Engine inlet equipped with a grounding (earthing) point and phone jack; installed on some aircraft.

Phone Jack
Communication interface located at the engine air intake grounding point.

Green System
One of three hydraulic systems on the A320; includes reservoir, accumulator, and ground service panel for centralized filling.

Yellow System
One of three hydraulic systems on the A320; includes reservoir, accumulator, and braking accumulator.

Blue System
One of three hydraulic systems on the A320; includes reservoir and accumulator.

Access Door 197CB
Access door for Green System hydraulic servicing and centralized filling; located at 19.17 m aft of nose, 1.27 m from centerline, 1.76 m mean height.

Access Door 198CB
Access door for Yellow System hydraulic servicing; located at 19.17 m aft of nose, 1.27 m from centerline, 1.76 m mean height.

Access Door 197EB
Access door for Blue System hydraulic servicing; located at 20.22 m aft of nose, 1.27 m from centerline, 1.76 m mean height.

Fuel System
Aircraft system covering refuel/defuel control panel, couplings, and overwing gravity refuel capabilities.

Refuel/Defuel Control Panel
Integrated panel for controlling refuel and defuel operations, located at Access Door 192MB.

Access Door 192MB
Access door on the aircraft fuselage providing access to the Refuel/Defuel Control Panel, positioned 16.4 m aft of nose on centerline at 1.8 m height.

Refuel/Defuel Coupling Left
Left wing refuel/defuel coupling (optional) located at Access Panel 522HB, 17.59 m aft of nose, 9.83 m left of centerline, 3.65 m height.

Access Panel 522HB
Access panel on left wing providing access to the left Refuel/Defuel Coupling.

Refuel/Defuel Coupling Right
Right wing refuel/defuel coupling located at Access Panel 622HB, 17.59 m aft of nose, 9.83 m right of centerline, 3.65 m height.

Access Panel 622HB
Access panel on right wing providing access to the right Refuel/Defuel Coupling.

Overwing Gravity Refuel Cap
Overwing gravity refuel cap positioned 19.1 m aft of nose, 12.4 m from centerline on both sides, 3.7 m height.

ISO 45
International standard for refuel/defuel couplings, specified for the right wing coupling.

RAT
Ram Air Turbine, referenced in the Ground Service Connections figure for the Electrical System.

Figure 5-4-3-991-007-A01
Figure showing Ground Service Connections for the RAT in Section 5-4-3.

Figure 5-4-4-991-001-A01
Figure showing External Power Receptacles (108VU, Access Door 121AL) in Section 5-

Overwing Gravity-Refuel Cap
A refueling cap located on the wing upper surface, with dimensions 9.83 m (32.25 ft) from aircraft centerline, 3.65 m (11.98 ft) aft of nose, and 19.1 m (62.66 ft) mean height from ground.

Refuel/Defuel Couplings
Couplings used for pressure refueling and defueling operations on the aircraft wings.

Right Wing Refuel/Defuel Coupling
A standard ISO 45, 2.5 in. refuel/defuel coupling located on the right wing.

Left Wing Refuel/Defuel Coupling
An optional standard ISO 45, 2.5 in. refuel/defuel coupling located on the left wing.

ISO 45 Standard
International standard specification for the 2.5 in. refuel/defuel coupling interface used on the aircraft.

Refuel Pressure
Maximum refuel pressure specification of 3.45 bar (50 psi) for the aircraft refueling system.

Average Flow Rate
Average refuel flow rate specification of 1250 l/min (330 US gal/min) for the aircraft refueling system.

Surge Tank Overpressure Protector
Overpressure protection device for the surge tank, accessed via panel 550CB (650CB), located at 20.36 m (66.80 ft) aft of nose, 14.9 m (48.88 ft) from centerline on both sides, and 4.32 m (14.17 ft) mean height from ground.

Inner Cell Overpressure Protector
Overpressure protection device for the inner fuel cell, accessed via panel 540HB (640HB), located at 19.5 m (63.98 ft) aft of nose, 9.19 m (30.15 ft) from centerline on both sides, and 4.1 m (13.45 ft) mean height from ground.

NACA Vent Intake
National Advisory Committee for Aeronautics vent intake for fuel tank ventilation, accessed via panel 550AB (650AB), located at 19.8 m (64.96 ft) aft of nose, 13.7 m (44.95 ft) from centerline on both sides, and 4.02 m (13.19 ft) mean height from ground.

Access Panel 550CB
Access panel for the surge tank overpressure protector, also designated as 650CB.
